decision_note: Closed by a logged decision, which is what the gate requires. The decision is no. This record exists so the gate is CLOSED rather than open-and-unexamined; it does not authorise anything.

evidence_files.note: Renders all three handoffs with approved_for_live_action false; performs none.

gate_test_status: The gate-5 test passes because nothing has recorded a performed live call, not because this gate was cleared for live action. It fails the moment a live call is recorded without an approval record.
handoff_condition: Live network calls, external writes, credentials, production databases, emails, dashboards, publishing, or model calls with sensitive data require an approval record.
preconditions_to_reopen: Real fetchers implemented in step 2, reading credentials from the environment only.
A second fixture set covering 401/403/429/timeout/empty-200, with expected detections declared.
A named recipient for the Slack and email actions, and a stated retention position for what is sent.
A suitability review of the model prompt, which asks for actionable insights on a financial question.
residual_risk: A deny is not a safety guarantee. Nothing in the pipeline enforces this decision at runtime -- it is enforced by step 2 refusing live mode and by the gate-5 test, both of which are code that could be changed.
voids_if: Any edit to the recipe or its six step scripts, any change to the fixture corpus, or any implementation of live mode voids this decision and requires a fresh one.
why_denied: Live mode is unimplemented: step 2 hard-stops before any fetch, so an approval would authorise a capability that does not exist.
No credentials are configured. Approving would mean approving in principle, which is the checkbox the gate exists to prevent.
The frozen corpus explicitly does not cover upstream HTTP failure modes (401, 403, 429, timeout, empty 200). The failure behaviour of a live run has never been exercised.
Two of the three declined actions are outward-facing and irreversible once sent: a Slack message and an email. The third generates investment-flavoured prose from a model.
